documents.title: Divi Games: play as your IronDivi wallet, and deposit or withdraw tDIVI
documents.content:
# Divi Games: play as your IronDivi wallet, and move tDIVI in and out

Divi Games (https://games.divi.domains) runs on its own test side chain, `divi-games-testnet-1`. It charges no fees and uses test coins only: GOLD for games, and tDIVI bridged from the Divi testnet. Nothing on it has real value.

## Playing as your wallet

Every game page (Tic-tac-toe, Blackjack, Tower defense) has **Play as your wallet** with three buttons:

- **Browser Wallet**: the IronDivi Browser Wallet add-on asks you to approve one message. If the add-on is not installed, the page links to it. Set the add-on to testnet for Divi Games: its popup is **purple on testnet** and **Divi red on mainnet**, and switching between them asks for your wallet password (the one you unlock it with, not your recovery phrase). Since version 0.0.2 every account in it also has mainnet (D) addresses. Since version 0.0.3 (https://github.com/bshuler/irondivi-browser-extension/releases/tag/v0.0.3) an incoming payment, such as a testnet faucet drip, shows in its history at once as **Pending · 0/6 confirmations** and counts up as blocks arrive; every history row links to the transaction on the services.divi.domains explorer, which lists it once it is in a block (about a minute). Since version 0.0.9 (https://github.com/bshuler/irondivi-browser-extension/releases/tag/v0.0.9) it also pays script addresses (mainnet addresses starting with 6, testnet ones with 8 or 9), such as the DNSDivi (divi.cx) registration address, and testnet addresses starting with x. When it refuses a payment a site asked for, for example one over the spending limit of 10% of the balance, the site is told only that the wallet cannot make the payment; the popup shows the owner the real reason, and the limits can be changed in Settings, Security. To upgrade it, unzip the new release over the same folder and press Reload on chrome://extensions; removing the add-on deletes its wallets.
- **Web Wallet**: the IronDivi Web Wallet (https://services.divi.domains/testnet/wallet/) opens in a new window. Unlock it and approve the message. If no message appears once the wallet is unlocked, press **Send the request** on the game page.
- **Telegram**: the page shows a `/sign testnet …` command. Send it to @divi_wallet_bot, tap **Sign in Wallet**, sign in the wallet that opens, tap **Copy** under the signature, and paste it into the page.

You sign **one** message, once. It reads `Divi Games session: key <K> may play as this address on divi-games-testnet-1 until <date>`. `<K>` is a new **session key** the page makes and keeps in your browser. Until that date (at most 30 days) the page plays as your wallet's address without asking again: your games, GOLD and wins belong to your wallet address.

A session key can only **play games and use the GOLD faucet**. It cannot send GOLD or tDIVI or withdraw anything; the chain refuses with "session keys can only play games". Signing the message moves no coins and costs nothing.

**Disconnect** ends the session on the chain, so the key is worthless even if someone copied it. The owner can also end any of their sessions early. Without that, a session simply expires on its date.

Without a wallet you can still play: the page makes a **play key** of its own, kept in your browser.

## Depositing tDIVI

The bridge is on for `divi-games-testnet-1`. Its Divi testnet address is `y7SwXAHzGzAb2hpn5Ueb8kwuVAQuBwqHF3`, and the chain also publishes it as `bridge_address` at https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/info. Once a wallet is connected, each game page shows a **tDIVI bridge** panel with your tDIVI balance and the deposit address. Send testnet DIVI to it with your game address written as the transaction's **memo (OP_RETURN)**:

- **Web Wallet**: the page's link opens the wallet's Send panel with the bridge address, the amount, and your address as the OP_RETURN already filled in. Check and press Send.
- **Telegram**: the page shows `/send <bridge address> <amount> <your address>`. Send it to @divi_wallet_bot and confirm in the wallet.
- **Browser Wallet**: it cannot add a memo yet, so use the Web Wallet or Telegram for deposits.

The chain credits the address in the first OP_RETURN when it is a valid testnet address (and not the bridge address itself). A deposit with no usable memo does not mint: it is held for the operator, who returns it by hand, so always include the memo, even to credit your own address. The chain mints only when two separate Divi nodes report the same deposit in the same block; a single deposit over 1000 DIVI is held, and minting pauses once 10000 DIVI has been minted in 24 hours. One testnet DIVI gives one tDIVI, credited after 6 confirmations on the Divi testnet.

## Withdrawing tDIVI

On the game page, open **tDIVI bridge**, enter an amount and a Divi testnet address and press **Withdraw**. Your wallet signs the withdrawal itself (the session key cannot). The chain takes the tDIVI from your balance straight away and adds the withdrawal to a queue with a number.

## How a withdrawal is paid

Payouts are **not automatic**. The operator pays each queued withdrawal by hand, from the bridge's own Divi testnet address, and then records the payment on the chain:

1. The operator's payout tool builds a Divi testnet transaction that sends the withdrawal's amount to the address you gave, with any change going back to the bridge address. The bridge's key is kept in the operator's password manager and never written to disk.
2. Once that transaction is broadcast, the operator records it on the gamechain with the sequencer's key: withdrawal *N* was paid in Divi transaction *T*. Only the sequencer can do this.

You can check a withdrawal yourself:

- https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/games/bridge?view=queue lists the withdrawals still waiting to be paid.
- https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/games/bridge?id=N shows withdrawal *N*: its amount and address, and once paid, `paid: true` and `paid_txid`, the Divi testnet transaction that paid it. Look that up in a Divi testnet explorer or your wallet.
- https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/games/bridge?outpoint=TXID:VOUT shows whether a deposit output has been credited.

The chain refuses to record a second payment for the same withdrawal, but it cannot see Divi itself: until a payment is recorded the withdrawal still shows as queued. All of this is testnet money with no value.

documents.title: Divi Games: play the tic-tac-toe bot or watch two bots, approve its moves or pick another
documents.content:
# Divi Games: play the tic-tac-toe bot, or watch two bots play

Tic-tac-toe on Divi Games (https://games.divi.domains/play/tictactoe/) has a bot for the second seat. At the top of the lobby:

- **Play the bot** makes a table where you are X and the bot is O.
- **Watch two bots** makes a table where a bot plays each side.

Bot tables have **no stake** (stake 0), so you need no GOLD and nobody needs the faucet.

## Let the bot join your own table

Made a table with **New table** and no one has joined? Open it and press **Let the bot join**; Bot O takes the O seat and the bot panel plays it. On a table with a stake the bot puts up the same stake, so if Bot O holds too little GOLD it first claims 1000 GOLD from the faucet for its own address, then joins. The faucet gives each address GOLD only once in a while; if Bot O claimed recently the page says the block at which it can claim again, so try again then or make a table with a smaller stake. The bot never loses, so on a staked table the best you can do is a draw, which returns both stakes.

The bot looks at every way the game can go (a full game-tree search called negamax), so it never loses; two bots always draw.

## The bot explains every move before it plays

Before each bot move the bot panel shows:

- **the move** it wants to play, drawn faintly on the board, with a badge saying whether that move leads to a win, a draw or a loss with best play;
- **Why**: one sentence, such as "Blocks X: they would win on the top left next move." or "Takes the centre: it sits on four of the eight lines.";
- **Then**: the reply it expects from the other side, also drawn faintly.

## You decide what it plays

- **Approve** plays the move on offer.
- **Pick another** puts the bot's next-best move on offer instead, with its own reason and outcome. Press it again to keep going down the list ("Pick another (2 of 7)").
- **Tap any free square**, or one of the small move buttons under the panel, to put that square on offer. Then press Approve to play it. You can make the bot play a losing move this way; its badge says "loss".
- **Pace** chooses who presses Approve: "Ask me before each move" waits for you; "Play every 3, 8 or 15 seconds" counts down and plays the move on offer by itself. Picking another move starts the count again.

The **Moves** list keeps every move with its reason and marks it **approved**, **your pick** or **auto** (played by the timer). When a game ends, **Play again** starts a new one.

## How it works on the chain

The bot is not part of the chain. Bot X and Bot O are two separate players, each with its own key made from its own **12-word recovery phrase** (BIP-39, the same kind the IronDivi wallets use). Each bot's address is address 0 of its phrase on the path m/44'/1'/0'/0/0, so typing a bot's 12 words into the IronDivi Browser, Web or Telegram wallet opens that same address. The page keeps the two phrases in the browser's storage. The bots sign the same create, join and move transactions a person signs, so the chain treats bot games like any other game, and every bot move is public in the Chain explorer. Play the bot creates a table with stake 0 reserved for Bot O, and Bot O joins it. The bot code is web/play/tictactoe/bot.js in the divi_games repository; the tutorial "Build tic-tac-toe" (https://services.divi.domains/tutorials/build-tic-tac-toe/#bot) walks through it. Examples: tables 311080e52f0e251b and d1e74b2af5ce57bf on the live chain are two-bot games that ended in a draw.

## The "On the chain" panel

Beside the board (under it on a phone) the **On the chain** panel shows what each play does on the two chains, live:

- **The chain heads**: the newest block of the **Divi Games sidechain** and the newest **Divi testnet** block the sidechain's sequencer has seen. Divi is the main chain; the sidechain is a separate chain that runs the games and anchors itself to Divi.
- **The two players**: each seat's address and its key path. For a bot, **Show the 12 words** reveals that bot's recovery phrase (it is a testnet bot with no real coins, but treat a real phrase as secret). A seat whose key is not in this browser says "A key this browser does not hold; only its owner can sign for this seat". The chain only accepts a move signed by the key in that seat.
- **What each move did**: one entry per transaction (create, join, each move). Each goes **Signed → Sidechain block → Sealed on Divi**, and its badge reads "Signed, sending…", "In the mempool", "In block #N" and finally "Sealed on Divi". The entry shows who signed it and the nonce, the **txid**, the **signature** with "✓ checked here" (the page checks it itself), the **block** number, block hash, **state root**, the sequencer that made the block, the Divi tip at that moment, the **events** the game module emitted (tictactoe.created, tictactoe.joined, tictactoe.moved, tictactoe.finished), and **The exact bytes that were signed** (the txid is the SHA-256 of that text).
- **Divi anchor**: moves are not Divi transactions, and GOLD is a sidechain token. Soon after a sidechain block holds a move, the sequencer writes one Divi testnet transaction with an OP_RETURN holding the newest block's height, hash and state root, which seals that block and every block before it. It sends at most one such anchor per Divi block (about one a minute), so a move is usually sealed within a minute or two; a quiet chain with no moves is still sealed every 300 blocks. Until then a move says "Being written to Divi"; afterwards it shows "Sealed on Divi" and links the Divi transaction. Example: on 2026-10-24 table ec069c0b2e3f1713 ended at sidechain block 5583 and the anchor for block 5584 was in a Divi block about two minutes later.

Every txid, block, address and anchor in the panel is a link: sidechain ones open the raw JSON from https://games.divi.domains/chain, Divi ones open the IronDivi testnet explorer, explorer2 (https://services.divi.domains/testnet/explorer2/). An anchor there is a Divi transaction that pays almost all of its input back to the same address (the sequencer's anchor address; the small difference is the fee) and has one more output, #0 "nulldata" with 0.00 DIVI: that zero-value OP_RETURN output is the seal, holding the sidechain block's height, hash and state root. explorer2 labels that output **Sidechain anchor** and links it back to the block it seals ("Divi Games block #N", which opens https://games.divi.domains/explorer/block/N). It knows where to link because Divi Games is registered on Divi (see "Sidechains on Divi"). The older explorer at /testnet/explorer/ does not show the nulldata output, so an anchor looks like a pointless payment to itself there; use explorer2.

## Troubleshooting

- **The bot does not move**: the pace is "Ask me before each move", so it waits for Approve. Choose a timed pace to let it play by itself.
- **I cannot find an older game**: the lobby lists open and running tables and the four newest finished ones. Press **Show older** under the list to see the rest, or open a table by its link (…/play/tictactoe/#<table id>).
- **I want to play for GOLD**: Play the bot and Watch two bots are always free. Make a New table with a stake, then play a person or press Let the bot join on it.

documents.title: Divi Games: the block explorer, search, transaction and address pages, and why there are empty blocks
documents.content:
# The Divi Games block explorer

The Divi Games sidechain (divi-games-testnet-1) has its own block explorer at https://games.divi.domains/explorer (the **Chain** link on the site).

## Search
The search box takes a block number, a 64-character transaction id, or an address (dt1...). It opens the block, transaction or address page.

## Transaction page
https://games.divi.domains/explorer/tx/<txid> shows what the transaction did (for example "tictactoe move" or "faucet GOLD"), who signed it, the block it is in, and whether that block is sealed on Divi yet. When it is sealed, the page links to the Divi transaction that sealed it on the Divi explorer (services.divi.domains).

## Address page
https://games.divi.domains/explorer/address/<address> shows the address's token balances (such as GOLD) and the transactions it signed, newest first.

## Latest blocks and empty heartbeat blocks
The home page lists the latest transactions and the latest blocks that hold transactions. The chain makes a block every 2 seconds while there are transactions. When nothing happens it still makes one empty "heartbeat" block every 60 seconds, about 1,440 a day, to show it is alive. These are the blocks with 0 transactions.

Empty blocks are **not** swept into one record each day, and they are never deleted: each block carries the hash of the block before it, so removing one would break the chain. The explorer counts each run of empty blocks in one row ("N empty heartbeat blocks"). **Every block** (?all=1) shows every block, empty ones included, 50 per page.

## Sealed on Divi
The sidechain writes a small Divi transaction (an OP_RETURN starting DGCH) that records the hash of its newest block. One such anchor seals that block and every block before it. A block with a player transaction is usually sealed within a minute or two. The explorer marks sealed blocks and links each anchor to its Divi transaction.
On the Divi explorer (explorer2) the anchor transaction's nulldata output is labelled **Sidechain anchor** and links back to the Divi Games block it seals, so the link works in both directions. Under **Sealed on Divi** the Chain page also links to Divi Games's registration on Divi and to the **Sidechains on Divi** list.

documents.title: Sidechains on Divi: how a sidechain registers on Divi (DVSC1) and how explorers link to it
documents.content:
# Sidechains on Divi: the sidechain registry

A sidechain seals its blocks on Divi by writing small Divi transactions (anchors) with an OP_RETURN output, shown as **nulldata** in explorers. To tell the world it exists, and to let Divi explorers link its anchors back to its own explorer, a sidechain **registers** on Divi with one ordinary Divi transaction. There is no company or server that approves it: the record is on the Divi chain for anyone to read.

## The registration transaction

- It sends **0.01 DIVI** (1,000,000 satoshis) to the **registry address**. Nobody holds a key for that address (its hash160 is the hash160 of the text "Divi sidechain registry v1"), so those coins stay there. The small payment is what keeps the list free of spam and lets an explorer find every registration by asking a Divi node for the registry address's transactions. Testnet registry address: yHkf3MUN4zLoXa84X1AXNvrSVg1TkF5cBh. Mainnet registry address: DRuuiWyxgKqJPKvcrGrnXGBgtgveBuGLig.
- It has exactly one **nulldata** (OP_RETURN) output holding the record, at most 599 bytes. Divi relays one OP_RETURN output per transaction, up to 603 bytes of script.
- All its inputs come from **one address**, the sidechain's **anchor address**: the address that pays for its anchors.

## The record (DVSC1)

The first line is `DVSC1`, then one `key=value` per line. This is the real Divi Games record:

```
DVSC1
id=divi-games-testnet-1
name=Divi Games
anchor=DGCH
genesis=96795518c5e69f4c07588b3373fc1c962889ff6ed107323b5a19b262029f917d
site=https://games.divi.domains
tx=/explorer/tx/{txid}
block=/explorer/block/{height}
address=/explorer/address/{address}
api=https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1
faucet=/play/tictactoe/
docs=/learn
```

- Required: **id** (the chain id), **name**, **anchor** (the tag its anchors start with, such as DGCH), **genesis** (hash of its first block), **site** (its home page; a sidechain with nothing to visit has no reason to register).
- Optional links: **tx**, **block**, **address** (explorer links with `{txid}`, `{height}`, `{address}` filled in), **api**, **faucet**, **docs**, **wallet**. A value starting with `/` is a path on `site`. Explorers only follow http and https links.

## What makes it authoritative

- The address that pays for the registration is the sidechain's anchor address. Only that address's key can make a registration for it, so a copycat cannot claim another chain's anchors.
- The **newest** registration from an address replaces the older ones, so a sidechain updates its links by registering again.
- A Divi transaction counts as an anchor of a registered sidechain only if it is paid by that anchor address and its nulldata starts with the registered tag. For Divi Games (tag DGCH) the anchor is 77 bytes: "DGCH", version 1, the block height, the block hash and the state root.

## Where to see it

- **Sidechains on Divi**: https://services.divi.domains/testnet/explorer2/sidechains lists every registered sidechain with its links, chain id, anchor tag, genesis block, anchor address and the registration transaction. The explorer2 home page links to it ("Sidechains on Divi →"). The mainnet list is at https://services.divi.domains/explorer2/sidechains (no sidechain is registered on mainnet yet).
- On a **registration** transaction, explorer2 labels the nulldata output **Sidechain** and shows the record with its links, and says whether it is the sidechain's current registration.
- On an **anchor** transaction, explorer2 labels the nulldata output **Sidechain anchor** and links to the sidechain block it seals, for example "Divi Games block #5,760", which opens https://games.divi.domains/explorer/block/5760. That block's page links back to the Divi transaction ("Sealed on Divi").

## Divi Games is registered

Divi Games (divi-games-testnet-1) registered on Divi testnet in transaction a80ff9cc3eb9e79faf8a896a15083e4cd4a877a402d6455773b31bc14868179c, paid from its anchor address xw9aaoN8FBrQcesu8F29ZjL6irKxyXpRRZ. Its API reports it as `registration` in https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/info, and its Chain page links to it.

## Registering your own sidechain

A Divi Games node registers with `divi-gamechain register --name ... --site ... [--tx ... --block ... --address ... --api ... --faucet ... --docs ... --wallet ...] --broadcast`, run while the node is running. Without `--broadcast` it only prints the record. Any other sidechain can register the same way by building a Divi transaction with the same shape: 0.01 DIVI to the registry address, one DVSC1 nulldata output, all inputs from its anchor address.

documents.title: Divi Games: game rules (tic-tac-toe, blackjack, tower defense, faucet) and the dates they change, including 2 November 2026
documents.content:
# Divi Games rules, and the dates they change

The Divi Games chain (divi-games-testnet-1, https://games.divi.domains) changes some rules on a fixed date. A rule change applies to actions in blocks from that time on; games already started keep their earlier rules where noted.

## The games today
- **Tic-tac-toe**: pick a stake (0 is a free game, at most 1000 GOLD). The winner gets both stakes, a draw refunds both, and if a player stops moving for five minutes the other may claim the win. Until someone joins, the creator can press **Cancel table** to get the stake back.
- **Blackjack**: bets 1 to 100 GOLD; a natural pays 3:2, any other win 1:1; the dealer stands on every 17. The house has 5 minutes to deal your card, or the hand closes as `house_timeout` and pays its best result (2.5x the stake, 2x on a doubled hand) through **Claim payout**. Ten minutes without a move and the hand stands on the cards you have.
- **Tower defense**: place towers (arrow, cannon, frost, sniper) on the board and press **Submit score** when the run ends. Each week the ten best scores share a prize pool; only a player's best run counts.
- **GOLD faucet**: 1000 GOLD, once an hour per address, measured in block time.

## 25 October 2026
- The faucet and game timeouts count block time (the time stamped on each block), not a number of blocks.
- From 08:00 UTC: at most 4 faucet claims per block (a claim past that fails with "try again in a few seconds"); a session key may stake only GOLD and at most 5000.00 GOLD over its life; a blackjack bet names the hash-chain card that deals it, a late house pays, an idle hand stands.

## 26 October 2026
- Each faucet pays at most 2000 claims per UTC day across every address ("has paid out its 2000 claims for today"; try again after midnight UTC).
- A session key can no longer fund the blackjack house.
- tDIVI bridge: a withdrawal must be at least 0.1 DIVI, and one address can make one withdrawal a minute.

## 2 November 2026 00:00 UTC
- **Tower defense, second tower set.** The arrow is unchanged. The cannon does 50 damage instead of 36 and fires more often; frost costs 70 gold instead of 90, does 6 damage instead of 4 and slows for longer; the sniper does 180 damage instead of 110 and fires a little more often. The two toughest creeps wear **armour** (6 points on the tank, 10 on the boss) that comes off every hit, which blunts the arrow's small hits most, so a mix of towers beats a field of arrows.
- A run keeps the tower stats it started with. From then on only runs started under the new stats enter the weekly leaderboard; an older run can still be submitted but does not rank.
- **Leaderboard ties** go to the run submitted first.
- **One prize per Telegram account.** Addresses linked to the same Telegram account count once on the tower-defense board, at their best rank; the others leave the board and the next player moves up, so linking more addresses cannot win more prizes. Unlinked addresses each count on their own.
- **The GOLD faucet gets two modes.** *Slow drip* is the usual mode: anyone can claim under the limits above. If addresses with no Telegram link make 100 claims within about two minutes, the faucet switches to *fast drip* for one hour and pays only addresses linked to a Telegram account; other claims fail with "the GOLD faucet is in fast-drip mode until …". Link an address by logging in with Telegram at https://games.divi.domains/account and linking it; the site records the link on chain. A linked address can always claim, in either mode, and skips the per-block and daily limits, but every address linked to one Telegram account shares one claim an hour, so linking more addresses does not give more GOLD. On chain the account appears only as a hash; anyone can see that linked addresses share it.
- **Tic-tac-toe open tables expire.** A table nobody joins within 24 hours can no longer be joined and the lobby hides it. Anyone may press **Cancel table (refunds its creator)** on it; the stake always goes back to the player who made the table.

The course *Using Divi*, lesson 3, at https://games.divi.domains/learn/using-divi/03-gold-and-your-first-game covers the games for players; *Game money* covers stakes and the faucet.

documents.title: Testnet DIVI faucet (tDIVI): limits, slow and fast drip, staking winnings only, Telegram-linked addresses, activity feed
documents.content:
# The testnet DIVI faucet (tDIVI)

The testnet faucet at https://services.divi.domains/testnet/faucet/ gives free testnet DIVI (coins with no value, for practising on the Divi test network). It is a different faucet from the Divi Games GOLD faucet.

## What it pays
- 1,000 testnet DIVI per payout, to an address starting with x or y. A mainnet D address does not work.
- It pays out only what its wallet has earned by staking. The coins it started with (3,890,000) stay in the wallet and keep staking, so the faucet never empties. When everything earned so far has been paid it answers "The faucet pays out only its staking winnings, and has paid out all it has earned so far. Please try again in a few hours."
- Its status page https://services.divi.domains/testnet/faucet/api/status shows the balance, how many payouts are available now, the current mode, and whether the wallet is staking.

## Slow drip (the usual mode)
Anyone can ask, under these limits:
- one payout per address every 24 hours;
- two payouts per network (IP address) every 24 hours;
- 50,000 testnet DIVI a day for the whole faucet, reset at 00:00 UTC.

## Fast drip (when it gets busy)
If 100 different networks ask within 2 minutes, the faucet switches to fast drip for one hour and pays only addresses linked to a Telegram account. Others get "The faucet is busy and paying only Telegram-linked addresses for the next … minute(s). Link this address at https://games.divi.domains/account to claim now."

## Telegram-linked addresses
Log in with Telegram at https://games.divi.domains/account and link your address there. The faucet counts the link straight away: it asks the Divi Games site, and from 2 November 2026 also reads the link from the Divi Games chain. A linked address can always claim, in slow or fast drip, and skips the network and daily limits. Each Telegram account gets one payout every 24 hours, whichever of its addresses asks ("Your Telegram account has already had its allotment").

## Faucet activity
The faucet page has a "Faucet activity" list, newest first: Sent (a 1,000 payout and who it went to), Received (coins returned or sent in), Stake (a staking reward, usually 166) and Lottery (a lottery win). Each line links to the transaction in the testnet explorer. The same list is at https://services.divi.domains/testnet/faucet/api/activity and refreshes every 30 seconds.

## Other refusals
- "This address has already received funds. Please wait … minute(s)": the 24-hour address limit.
- "Too many faucet requests from your network": that network has had its 2 payouts in the last 24 hours.
- "The faucet has reached its daily payout limit. Please try again after 00:00 UTC, or link this address …": the 50,000 daily budget is spent; a linked address can still claim.

Please send unused coins back to the faucet's return address yJehBfdK9KbrwPRjYrzkrPES9uG5nFLjY4. The tutorial *Get Testnet DIVI* walks through it: https://services.divi.domains/tutorials/testnet-faucet/

documents.title: Divi Games: the season market, trade by hand in the browser or run the example Python bot
documents.content:
# Divi Games: the season market, by hand in the browser or with a bot

A trading season on Divi Games is a market game: everyone who joins starts level with the same season-only tokens, S<n>GOLD and S<n>DIVI (in season 1, S1GOLD and S1DIVI: 1000 of each), and trades them against each other on an order book. The leaderboard marks each portfolio at the last trade price. Season tokens are worth nothing outside the season; nothing real is at stake. A house market-maker bot quotes both sides, so there is always someone to trade with. When a season ends the next starts on the very next block.

## You do not need a bot: trade in the browser

Open the season market at https://games.divi.domains/play/market/ (the market page links to it as **Trade in season N**).

1. **Join.** A fresh address sees **Join the season**. Press it; after the next block you hold the starting S<n>GOLD and S<n>DIVI. Each address can join once per season.
2. **Place an order.** Choose **Buy** or **Sell**, type a **price** in S<n>GOLD per S<n>DIVI and an **amount** in S<n>DIVI. The price takes up to 10 decimals, the same as the book shows, so clicking a row of the book fills in its exact price, and typing a book price back, for example 1.0899999999, gives that same price. The page refuses an order you cannot fund before signing, and shows the chain's reason if the chain refuses it.
3. **Watch and cancel.** An order that meets the other side trades at once, at the resting order's price, and shows in **Recent trades**. The rest waits under **Your open orders**; **Cancel** takes it off the book and returns what it locked.

The page trades with the testnet play key kept in the browser (the same key the games use). A connected IronDivi wallet cannot trade here, because the chain does not let a session key trade.

## Or run a bot: the example Python bot

A bot does the same three things automatically on every block. The site hosts a ready-to-run example in Python: the page https://games.divi.domains/bots/python/ explains it and has a **Download the bot (.zip)** button (https://games.divi.domains/bots/python/divi-games-python-bot.zip, which unzips to a divi-games-python-bot folder holding README.md, market_bot.py, divigames.py and test_bot.py; each file can also be downloaded alone). It needs Python 3.10 or newer and nothing else: it uses only the standard library, so there is nothing to pip install. It runs on Mac, Linux and Windows (on Windows type python instead of python3). It quotes both sides of the book around the last trade price (3 levels a side, 1 DIVI each, 2% spread by default) and re-quotes when the price moves.

    # unzip the download, then in the divi-games-python-bot folder:
    python3 market_bot.py --key-file ~/.divi-games/py.key --dry-run --once   # look first
    python3 market_bot.py --key-file ~/.divi-games/py.key                      # trade

On first run it creates a testnet key file (mode 0600) and joins the live season by itself, so no coins are needed. Ctrl-C stops it and cancels its open orders unless --keep-orders is given. Change ladder() in market_bot.py to change the strategy. To trade as the browser player instead, export the play key from the game page and save it as the key file with chmod 600. The divi_games repository also has the same bot in JavaScript (bots/js) and Rust (bots/rust).

## Limits

100 open orders per address, 5 transactions a second per IP, and an order that would trade with your own is refused. Prices on the wire are S<n>GOLD base units per whole S<n>DIVI times 10^8.

The course "Trading bots and seasons" (https://games.divi.domains/learn/trading-bots-and-seasons) covers the order book, seasons and writing a bot.

documents.title: Divi Games: run a verifying node (follower) on the game sidechain, admitted by a certificate from the operator's private CA, removed by its revocation list
documents.content:
# Divi Games: run a verifying node on the game sidechain

The Divi Games sidechain (testnet, pinned to Divi testnet) has one sequencer, the operator's node on games.divi.domains, which orders transactions and signs blocks. A **verifying node** (a follower, `divi-gamechain follow`) fetches every block from the sequencer and checks it before storing it, so a sequencer that signs a block its own rules do not produce is caught.

## Who may run one

Node runners are admitted by **certificate**. The operator keeps a private certificate authority (CA) and signs one certificate per runner. The sequencer's peer port, games.divi.domains:7420, speaks only TLS with client certificates and trusts that CA alone: a connection with no certificate, or a certificate another CA signed, is refused during the TLS handshake, before any request is read. The block feed holds nothing secret (the same blocks are public at https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/); the certificate decides who may be a runner.

To become a runner:

1. Make your own key and a certificate request; the key never leaves your machine:
   `openssl req -new -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -nodes -keyout runner.key -out runner.csr -subj "/CN=<your name>"` then `chmod 600 runner.key`.
2. Send runner.csr to the operator. They sign it (a client-only certificate, valid one year) and send back runner.crt together with peer-ca.crt, the CA's certificate (not secret; your node uses it to check the sequencer's own certificate).
3. Write a config and start the node: `divi-gamechain --config runner.toml --data-dir ./chain follow`, with
   `[follow]` upstream = "https://games.divi.domains:7420", sequencer = the sequencer address shown at https://games.divi.domains/chain/v1/info, cert = "runner.crt", key = "runner.key", ca = "peer-ca.crt". The node's own read API listens on 127.0.0.1:7410 by default.

## What the follower checks

On its first run it fetches the genesis and refuses it unless the chain id matches and the sequencer is the one pinned in `follow.sequencer`. Then for every new block: the height is head + 1 and prev_hash is the head's hash; the block is signed by the pinned sequencer; re-running the block's transactions on the follower's own state gives the same tx_root, state_root, receipts and events. Only then is the block stored.

## Reading its status

The follower's `/v1/info` has a `follow` field:
- `state: "following"` with `checked_ms`: it is up to date and every block passed.
- `state: "halted"` with `bad_block` and `error`: a block failed a check; it stores nothing more. This is the alarm a runner exists to raise.
- `state: "unreachable"`: a network error; it retries by itself.

## What a follower does not do

It serves the same read API as the sequencer, so players and tools can point at it, but it holds no sequencer key: it answers 503 to /v1/tx (sending transactions) and runs no house, anchor or bridge task. It catches a dishonest block; it cannot make blocks or move funds.

## Removing a runner: the revocation list

The operator removes a runner by revoking its certificate; the CA then signs a new revocation list (a standard X.509 CRL). Only the CA's key can sign one, so any node may pass it on and every node checks it itself. A node takes a list only if the CA signed it (a look-alike CA with the same name is refused) and its CRL number is higher than the one it holds (so an old list cannot un-revoke anyone). The sequencer serves its list at /peer/v1/crl on the peer port; every follower fetches it once a minute, stores it as peer-ca.crl in its data directory, and also refuses an upstream whose own certificate is on it.

New connections are checked against the list during the TLS handshake. Open connections are re-checked a few at a time: every cycle (peer.cycle_ms, default 10 s) the node checks the next peer.checks_per_cycle (default 16) of them and closes any now revoked, so the work per cycle stays fixed as the network grows. A new list is picked up without a restart.

## The gate will change

The private CA is today's gate. The plan, once the network is large enough, is to admit a runner while it controls an address holding 10,000,000 DIVI instead of a certificate, re-checked with the same per-cycle budget; that is not built yet. Followers serving each other is not built either, so every follower connects to the sequencer, and the sequencer still signs every block.

The course "The side-chain", lesson 6, covers the same ground: https://games.divi.domains/learn/the-side-chain

documents.title: Run every Divi Games game four ways: Docker stack, at home, IPFS and Tor
documents.content:
# Run every game four ways

The Run every game four ways course (games.divi.domains/learn/run-every-game) shows how to run each Divi Games game (tic-tac-toe, blackjack, tower defense, season market) yourself. Everything is testnet: GOLD is free from a faucet and worth nothing.

## The four ways

1. **Whole stack in Docker**: a Divi 3.0.0 testnet node, your own Divi Games side chain following it, the site and every game. From a checkout of the node repository (private for now): `cd local && docker compose up -d --build`, then open http://127.0.0.1:8080/play/. It is a separate chain with its own sequencer key and faucet; anchoring and the bridge are off. `docker compose down -v` deletes everything, the key too. Set `DIVI_RPC: ""` to run without a Divi node.
2. **Front end at home**: each game's public repository (DiviDomains/divi-games-tictactoe, -blackjack, -towerdefense, -market) runs with `npm start` or `node serve.mjs`, on ports 8081 to 8084, playing on the public testnet chain. `UPSTREAM=http://127.0.0.1:8080` plays on the way 1 chain instead. See the Run a game at home lesson.
3. **IPFS**: `npm run static` writes a plain-file copy to dist/ (the chain and site are named in meta tags; links are relative). `ipfs add -r --cid-version 1 -Q dist` prints the CID. Open it on your own IPFS node's gateway at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ipfs/<CID>/play/<game>/ (use 127.0.0.1, not localhost). Public gateways show the game but cannot play it, because the chain only answers pages from games.divi.domains and 127.0.0.1/localhost. `node static.mjs --chain http://127.0.0.1:8080/chain --site http://127.0.0.1:8080 dist-local` makes a copy that plays on your own chain. Copies show no rank line. Every CID on one gateway shares one play key, and any page opened there can read it. Pin the CID elsewhere to keep it online.
4. **Tor**: a compose file builds the four game containers (no published ports) and a tor container with one onion service each. Read an address with `docker compose exec tor cat /var/lib/tor/<game>/hostname` and open http://<address>.onion/play/<game>/ in Tor Browser on the Standard security level (Safest turns JavaScript off). Tor Browser forgets the play key when closed: connect a wallet or import a saved WIF. The onions volume holds the service keys; back it up privately, since whoever has hs_ed25519_secret_key can run that address.

## Still central

One sequencer at games.divi.domains orders and signs every block of the public chain and runs the faucet, the blackjack house and market seasons. serve.mjs reaches it over the ordinary internet, even on Tor. The leaderboard, explorer and account pages live on the site. Node runners' followers re-execute every block and serve the read API, but moves still go to the sequencer; producer rotation among runners is planned, not built. Whoever serves a page, the chain checks every move, so a changed page can only send moves the chain accepts.
